rationale: bugs_open/342 FOLLOW-UP, and it is a correction of my own approved work rather than an extension of it. Council trail 3626629a approved the refusal half on 2026-08-22; live traffic then showed that the ESCALATION half — shipped earlier by the same lane and reviewed on trail bb7f5d0e — files work items that its own router structurally cannot route. THE EVIDENCE, and it is 2 of 2: the producer has filed exactly two items since going live, `a6e00dcf` (2026-08-22 13:32, REAL production traffic on loans-application-tracker, not a test) and `a31da7f3` (18:03, my canary). BOTH were classified `route: "malformed"` by required-fields-missing-handler, both burned three attempts, both terminal `failed`. A 100% failure rate on a producer that logs `item filed` and whose orchestrations all read COMPLETED. CAUSE 1 — the items are unroutable. `required-fields-missing-handler`'s `classify` step resolves the page by `spec->>'page_name'` and the component by `spec->>'slot_name'` (read from the live agent row, the predicate is in its SQL). The producer supplied NEITHER, so the classifier returned component_id='', html_len=0, page_type='' and fell through to the malformed branch. CAUSE 2 — the keys cannot co-dedup. `check_required_fields_missing.go:180` keys on `required_fields_missing:<page_id>:<slot_name>`; this producer keyed on `<site_id>:<component function>`. Two producers, two key shapes, two items for one defect. BOTH CAUSES ARE ONE FALSE ASSUMPTION, and it was written in four places — the code comment, the bug file, concept register STY-057, and the APPROVED submission on bb7f5d0e: that reusing the item TYPE meant inheriting its router. **Reusing a type is not reusing its contract.** An item_type is a string; a router is the set of fields it reads and the key it dedupes on. The reuse_agent seat approved the reasoning, correctly — the reasoning was sound; what nobody checked was whether the artefact matched it, and the failure is invisible from the producing side because the insert succeeds and every orchestration completes. Recorded in WRONG_CALLS.md with the check that would have caught it on day one (read the consumer's own classify predicate, or watch one filed item for an hour). THE FIX. The emitter takes a `pageContext` (id, name, slot) and writes `page_name`/`slot_name` into the spec — the fields the router actually reads. With a page it takes the check's key shape EXACTLY so the two producers genuinely co-dedup, and sets `page_id` on the row (the column existed on the shared workItem struct and was simply never set). WITHOUT a page — the chrome surface, whose slots hang off the SITE and which a page-resolving router cannot classify by construction — the item is filed for a human at `needs_human_review`, which is the router's OWN park_* vocabulary, rather than handed over to burn three attempts. Deliberately NOT a phantom handler_agent: bugs_closed/291 established that an unregistered handler is born `blocked` and never claimed, which reads as a queue bug rather than as work waiting for a person. The routing decision is factored into `requiredFieldsMissingRouting` so the test exercises exactly what production runs — the emitter itself needs a database, and both defects are computable without one. Mutation-proven: routing chrome to the page-router fails two assertions, and a page-WITHOUT-slot taking the routed path fails a third (the classifier needs both, so half the context must not look like all of it). BLAST RADIUS AND WHAT IS NOT DONE: two existing items are left as the honest record rather than rewritten — the key shape changed, so the fixed code files a correctly-routed item next time either path runs, and hand-editing a queue row to prove my own fix is not evidence. The change is INERT until the next chassis roll. I have NOT touched required-fields-missing-handler: its behaviour on a malformed item (fail loudly rather than close silently) is correct and is what surfaced this.
submitter: bugfix_342_absent_required lane — correcting its own approved work after live traffic refuted two claims

plan.summary: Fix bugs_open/342's escalation: the items it files carry neither of the two spec fields its router resolves by, and key on a different shape from the sibling producer, so 2 of 2 items ever filed were classified malformed and parked. Supply the page context, adopt the check's key shape, and park the page-less chrome surface for a human instead of fake-routing it.

edits.rationale: The whole fix. spec gains page_name/slot_name (what classify reads); the key follows check_required_fields_missing.go:180 when a page is known so the two producers co-dedup; page_id is set on the row (the field existed, unset); and the page-less case is parked for a human rather than routed. The decision is factored so a test can exercise it without a database — the two defects are both decisions, not I/O.

Both edit branches already hold the PageInfo and the page_component row; one helper assembles the context from them. A helper rather than two literals because two branches filing one item type with different context is exactly how this defect arose.

Passes pageContext{} explicitly, with the reason at the call site: a chrome slot hangs off the site, so there is no page for classify to resolve and the emitter must park it rather than route it. Making the emptiness explicit and commented is the point — a caller reading this must not 'fix' it by inventing a page.
edits.sketch:
// pageContext{} — EMPTY, deliberately: a chrome slot hangs off the SITE
emitRequiredFieldsMissing(ctx, db, siteID, pageContext{}, &compID, slot, ...)

edits.rationale: Pins the contract that nothing asserted, which is why the defect shipped: the page-scoped key must equal the check's shape exactly, the page-scoped item must go to the router at status detected, the page-less item must NOT be handed to the router and must park at needs_human_review, and a page WITHOUT a slot must fall back rather than emit a half-formed page key. Mutation-proven on all three arms.

grounded_in: Live evidence, 2026-08-23: SELECT status, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='required_fields_missing' AND spec->>'detected_at'='render' → failed|2. Both items (a6e00dcf 13:32 real traffic on loans-application-tracker; a31da7f3 18:03 canary) show attempt_count=3 and the handler's triage recorded route:'malformed', component_id:'', html_len:0, page_type:''.

required-fields-missing-handler's classify step, read from the live agent_definitions row: `... FROM pages p CROSS JOIN item WHERE p.site_id = $1::uuid AND p.name = item.spec->>'page_name' ...` and the component resolved via the page — the two spec fields the producer never supplied.

check_required_fields_missing.go:180 — `ItemKey: fmt.Sprintf("required_fields_missing:%s:%s", pageID, slotName)`, against this producer's `<site_id>:<scopeKey>`; verified against live rows (the check's key segment resolves as a page id, mine as a site id).

The false claims being corrected, quoted from my own approved work: bug file and STY-057, 'the item type that ALREADY EXISTS for this defect, with a router already seeded (bugs_open/277)' and 'the item_key matches the check's so the two producers co-dedup'.
bugs_closed/291: an unregistered handler_agent is born `blocked` and never claimed — why the page-less case gets an EMPTY handler and needs_human_review rather than a plausible-looking handler name.
The router's own park_* steps set status `needs_human_review` (read from the live row), which is the vocabulary this change adopts rather than inventing one.
plan.risks: RISK 1: The page-less (chrome) branch now files items nothing will pick up automatically. That is intended and is the honest state — a page-resolving router cannot service them — but it means the chrome surface's findings accumulate for a human. Mitigated by the population: the chrome record fires on 0 rows today (re-measured at approval on trail 3626629a), so nothing accumulates until a chrome component with required source:llm fields is adopted, which is the same trigger already documented for arming the chrome refusal. RISK 2: The key shape changes, so an item filed by the OLD code and one filed by the new code for the same defect will not dedupe against each other. Blast radius is exactly two rows, both already terminal `failed`; they are deliberately left as the record rather than rewritten. RISK 3: page_id is now set on these rows where it was NULL before. Any consumer filtering on page_id IS NULL would see fewer rows — no such consumer was found, but the change is stated because a NULL becoming non-NULL is the kind of thing a census silently absorbs. RISK 4: The fix is INERT until the next chassis roll, so the producer keeps filing unroutable items until then. It has filed two in four days, both now terminal, so the accrual rate is low — but it is not zero and this is not a config flip that can be applied ahead of the binary. RISK 5: The test exercises the DECISION, not the insert (the emitter needs a database), so a regression that stops the caller PASSING the context — rather than one that mis-decides on it — would not be caught. The two callers are named in the plan and both go through one helper, which is the mitigation; the honest residual is stated rather than papered over.
